page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-44-lssd is a general-purpose server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 44 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 22 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 176.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. Storage is bundled with 3216 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity distributed across 8 local SSDs. No GPUs are included in this configuration, and it does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate average performance across most standard workloads. The single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests yield scores of 1624.38 and 36641.54, respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 2998.96 GB/sec, while large block uncached read and write speeds reach 111.44 GB/sec and 48.81 GB/sec. The instance demonstrates strong performance in specific areas, such as Geekbench image processing at 16162.0 and Passmark CPU encryption at 38720.91, both placing in the top 25%. However, text generation for large language models is a notable tradeoff; while prompt processing for a 70B model achieves 21.73 tokens/sec, text generation drops to 2.37 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c3-standard-44-lssd offers a balanced resource density of compute and high-speed local storage. The inclusion of 3.2 TB of local NVMe SSDs makes it highly suitable for database operations, which is supported by a Passmark database score of 18755.52 and Redis SET performance of 47.3 million operations per second. This server is optimized for workloads such as relational databases, local caching layers, static web serving with 40.85 GB/sec throughput, software compilation, and light to medium machine learning inference.

However, large-scale LLM text generation is a performance tradeoff, yielding only 2.37 tokens/sec on 70B models. The balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and high-speed local storage make this instance highly efficient for database operations, static web serving, and software compilation.
